record.paper_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
record.context_brief: Restricted differentiability of the interacting Lieb functional
record.original_question: For the interacting Lieb functional FL[n] in density functional theory, can one prove that FL[n] admits a derivative in a restricted or weak sense for every interacting ensemble v-representable density n in the set B, even though FL[n] is nowhere Gateaux differentiable on the full Banach space X? Any such result must identify physically meaningful perturbation directions that preserve particle number and keep perturbed densities inside the admissible density set S, while still making the directional derivative finite and linear on that restricted class.

evidence.quote: The existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in the general case thus still represents an open question.
Nevertheless, would FL[n] admit some weaker notion of a derivative in the subset B ⊂ S ? This would be sufficient for most of previous KS scheme considerations to hold.
A more general demonstration that at least relaxes all constraints on B would be necessary for most of previous KS scheme considerations to hold. This still represents an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ be the spatial domain and fix a particle number $N \in \mathbb{N}$. Consider the Banach space
$$X = L^1(\mathbb{R}^3) \cap L^3(\mathbb{R}^3),$$
equipped with the norm $\|n\|_X = \|n\|_{L^1} + \|n\|_{L^3}$, and the admissible set of $N$-particle densities
$$S = \Big\{ n \in X : n \ge 0 \text{ a.e.}, \ \int_{\mathbb{R}^3} n = N, \ \sqrt{n} \in H^1(\mathbb{R}^3) \Big\}.$$
For an electron–electron interaction $\hat{W}$, define the interacting Lieb (constrained-search) functional
$$F_L[n] = \inf\Big\{ \mathrm{Tr}\big(\hat{\Gamma}(\hat{T}+\hat{W})\big) : \hat{\Gamma} \text{ is an } N\text{-particle ensemble density matrix yielding } n \Big\},$$
where $\hat{T}$ denotes the kinetic-energy operator. Let
$$B \subset S$$
be the subset of densities that are interacting ensemble $v$-representable, i.e., densities $n \in S$ that arise as the ground-state density of $\hat{T}+\hat{W}+\sum_i v(x_i)$ for some external potential $v$ in a suitable dual class.

It is known that $F_L$ is convex on $S$ but is nowhere Gâteaux differentiable on $X$ in the usual sense.

Question. Does $F_L$ admit a derivative in some restricted (weak) sense at every $n \in B$? More precisely, does there exist a class $\mathcal{D}_n \subset X$ of admissible perturbation directions $\delta n$ such that:
(i) each $\delta n \in \mathcal{D}_n$ satisfies $\int \delta n = 0$ (particle-number preserving) and $n + t\,\delta n \in S$ for all sufficiently small $t > 0$;
(ii) the one-sided directional derivative
$$D_{\delta n} F_L[n] := \lim_{t \downarrow 0} \frac{F_L[n + t\,\delta n] - F_L[n]}{t}$$
exists and is finite for every $\delta n \in \mathcal{D}_n$;
(iii) the map $\delta n \mapsto D_{\delta n} F_L[n]$ is linear on $\mathcal{D}_n$ and represented by a (Kohn–Sham) potential $v_n$, in the sense that $D_{\delta n} F_L[n] = -\int v_n\, \delta n$ for all $\delta n \in \mathcal{D}_n$;
(iv) the class $\mathcal{D}_n$ is large enough to recover the conclusions normally drawn from Gâteaux differentiability of $F_L$ at $n$ (in particular, applicability to the Kohn–Sham scheme), without imposing further restrictions on $n$ beyond $n \in B$?
artifact.category_tag: Density functional theory / Lieb functional differentiability
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the Lieb functional admits a derivative in a restricted/weak sense at every interacting ensemble v-representable density remains open in general. Lammert (2007) showed the standard proof of Gâteaux differentiability is flawed and that $F_L$ is neither Gâteaux nor Fréchet differentiable in the usual sense; positive results exist only under extra restrictions (e.g. densities bounded away from zero with $L^2$ derivatives), or in special settings such as spinless fermions in one dimension (2025 work by Sutter et al.). No general result removing all restrictions on $B$ has been established.

status_evidence.title: Differentiability of Lieb functional in electronic density functional theory
status_evidence.snippet: A widely accepted proof that the Lieb functional is Gateaux differentiable at ensemble-V-representable densities is fallacious; the functional is not Gateaux differentiable in the normal sense.
status_evidence.claim: Lieb functional is not Gateaux differentiable in the usual sense; restricted derivative results require extra conditions on densities.

status_evidence.title: A rigorous formulation of density functional theory for spinless fermions in one dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Using the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem the constrained search functional has a unique subgradient at any density and is therefore Gâteaux differentiable.
status_evidence.claim: Positive differentiability results exist only in restricted settings such as 1D spinless fermions, not for the general 3D interacting Lieb functional.

status_evidence.title: Functional Derivatives and Differentiability in Density-Functional Theory
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the lack of Gateaux/Frechet differentiability of the Lieb functional and the open status of weaker notions of derivative.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a restricted-sense derivative for the Lieb functional on the full set of v-representable densities remains an open problem.
